I392640978042.note: Graduated from Decatur (Tex.) High School in 1957 and attended Decatur Baptist College (Army releases of 1958 and 1961; his 2024 obituary says Savoy, where his mother later lived). Entered the Army Feb 1958; basic at Fort Ord; 82nd Airborne jump school at Fort Bragg, Aug 1958; served in Germany; marched in President Kennedy's inaugural parade, Jan 1961; retired a Warrant Officer 3.

I392640984246.note: Nettie Tyson's younger sister (both are Albert Tyson's daughters in the 1940 census) and Joel G. Johnson's later wife. Rachel's tree had her as Bob's mother; his obituary names Nettie instead.

I392640985468.note: Married Winnie W. Bozarth in Texas in 1896. A stock buyer at Boswell in 1930 and later a farmer and rancher. His 1910 census entry gives his father’s birthplace as Arkansas and his mother’s as Mississippi but does not identify either parent; the former George Johnson and Marjorie Fail links are unproved.

I392640985854.note: The 1896 Lee County marriage index records Joel A. Johnson and Minnie or Winnie W. Bozanth or Bozarth. The 1920 household records Joel, Minnie, their children and his mother-in-law Florence Minton; its names and ages match the 1910 Winnie and Joel family. The joint headstone with Joel gives Winnie’s birth and death dates. The identity of her father and Florence’s earlier surname require more evidence.

I392640996589.note: Bob Johnson's mother. Army hometown releases name her Mrs. Nettie B. McCarter of Route 2, Sherman, Texas (1958) and Mrs. Nettie B. Tillery of Sadler, Texas (1961). She died a Tillery on 6 Feb 1980; her last home was Savoy and she is buried in Sunnyside Cemetery there.

I392657395404.note: Farmer at Oakes, Choctaw County, in 1940, aged 65, born in Texas.

I392657395681.note: Winona contractor for 40 years (Hanson & Nelton, then his own firm); built many of the city's homes and early stores. His 1942 draft card gives Minneiska as his birthplace; his 1952 obituary says Winona.

I392657396086.note: This person was previously attached as a parent of Joel Anderson Johnson, but no independently examined record has identified Joel’s parents. The former link and the person’s connection to Rachel remain unproved.

I392657396192.note: The proposed links from George Washington Johnson to Jonathan T., and from Jonathan T. to Joel Johnson, remain unproved. A Lakeport estate settlement lists several of Joel’s heirs but is not a complete list of his children. An original record naming George’s parents or confirming Jonathan’s parentage is needed.

I392657396441.n: William Johnston, Mbr House of Burgesses
I392657396441.note: A previous tree identified this Virginia William as the son of the Marquess of Annandale and Sophia Fairholm. Westminster Abbey records that their son Lord William died in 1721, aged 26, so he cannot be the Virginia man the tree gives a 1778 death. The Virginia man’s birth and parents require independent records; the proposed connection to Rachel is also unproved.

I392657396499.note: William Johnstone, 1st Marquess of Annandale, married Sophia Fairholm. Their son Lord William died in 1721; a previously attached Virginia man with a reported 1778 death is a different person. A connection to Rachel has not been established.

I392657396529.note: Westminster Abbey records Sophia’s death in 1716 and the burial of her son Lord William, who died in 1721. A former tree confused him with a Virginia William said to have died in 1778; the connection to Rachel has not been established. A portrait was published under her name in the 1894 Annandale Family Book; its original sitter has not independently been verified.

I392657398036.note: Parents Frederick and Elizabeth are explicitly named in George W. Hall’s 1884 county biography, pp. 1283–1284. Birth date conflict: biography prints 28 Feb 1825; existing tree has 25 Feb 1825. Exact day remains unresolved.

I392657428383.note: The family tree calls him Charles Hercules Bell. His shared marker with Mary Alice gives Charles H. Bell, 1873–1930. A 1949 certificate for Lee Hercules Bell names a father Charles H. Bell and mother Clara Shelton; whether that is this Charles remains unconfirmed.

X_edsr.note: Rural mail carrier at Rollingstone for 30 years (1903–1934) and mayor of the village from 1938 to 1948.

X_johanna.note: Birth, death and parents Jacob and Theresa are reported in her Winona Daily News 5 Mar 1967 obituary, transcribed on Find a Grave. Identification with Hannah, daughter of Jacob Johns and Theresa Kryzer in 1895 county biography, is probable: same parent names, nearby place, siblings Rose/George and exactly matching sibling counts. The extension to Jacob's parents relies on that probable identification.

X_henry.note: Rollingstone's postmaster before his brother John B. Rivers took over in 1886.

X_eliz.note: Came to America in 1860; ran a hotel in Rollingstone after her husband's death.

X_michel.note: Came to America in 1854 and settled on a farm in Winona County in 1855 (1913 county history).

X_johnfrisch.note: Taught school eight years, farmed the Frisch homestead on Oak Ridge, and was secretary of the Rollingstone Mutual Farmers Fire Insurance Company for 24 years.

X_maggie.note: Died at 31, fourteen days after the birth of her third child.

X_jacques.note: His 1906 memorial gives 28 October 1837; St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index gives 18 October 1836. His birth date remains unresolved. The 1883 county history names Jacob Frisch among the men who helped establish the Oak Ridge Catholic church.

X_annaspeltz.note: Her obituary says she and Jacques landed at Winona on 4 July 1864 and settled at Oak Ridge.

X_elizabeth_tyson.note: Albert Tyson's wife in the 1940 census at Oakes, Choctaw County, in the household with his daughters Nettie and Opal.

X_nel.note: Helen’s 1948 obituary identifies her as Mrs. Thomas S. Miller, formerly Helen Heffernan, and names the same two daughters recorded in 1920. The 1900 Heffernan household and a 1939 Social Security application support parents John H. Heffernan and Mary Shea. Her 1948 death index instead names Patrick Heffernan and Ellen Shea. The proposed parents are probable; the conflicting father’s name and her exact birth year remain unresolved. The Minnesota death index gives 15 January 1948 in Winona Township.

X_johnbrivers.note: Purchased a Norton township farm in 1866; opened his Rollingstone store in 1872; married Anna Heber on 29 Oct 1866. 1913 biography names Michael and Margaret (Adam) Rivers as parents.

X_annaheber.note: Married John B. Rivers on 29 Oct 1866; daughter of Nicholas Heber, named in his 1913 biography.

X_nicholasheber.note: Named as Anna Heber Rivers father in the 1913 biography of John B. Rivers. No dates or spouse identified.

X_johnhrivers.note: Educated at Winona State Normal School and Business College; grocery business in Winona with brother J. P.; returned to Rollingstone in 1896 to sell dry goods. Married Bertha Jung 10 Oct 1894.

X_matthewrivers.note: Worked in the family general store and as assistant postmaster. His 1913 biography names his wife as Kathryn Trisch, married 19 November 1907. Other family accounts use Katherine Frisch; the identification remains unresolved.

X_johnprivers.note: Named as a child of John B. and Anna (Heber) Rivers in the 1913 biography.

X_elizabethrivers.note: Named as a child of John B. and Anna (Heber) Rivers in the 1913 biography.

X_josephinerivers.note: Named as a child of John B. and Anna (Heber) Rivers in the 1913 biography.

X_berthajung.note: Married John H. Rivers on 10 Oct 1894; her parents are named in his contemporary 1913 biography.

X_johnjung.note: Rollingstone merchant; he and wife Margaretha Kohner are described as pioneers of 1855 in their son-in-law John H. Rivers’s biography.

X_margarethakohner.note: Named as mother of Bertha Jung Rivers in John H. Rivers’s 1913 biography.

X_andrewrivers.note: A 1913 biography gives John H. Rivers’s son Andrew a birth date of 10 December 1895. The Mayo physician Andrew Baptiste Rivers was born on 10 December 1894 according to a university memorial and a Navy register; the identification and the family path to Rachel remain research leads.

X_angelinerivers.note: Birth date and parents recorded in the contemporary 1913 biography of John H. Rivers.

X_jacobjohns1842.note: Probable father of Johanna Johns Rivers. His 1895 biography gives 5 August 1842, parents Jacob and Maggie (Jahn), marriage to Theresa Kryzer on 18 May 1868, and twelve children including Hannah, Rose and George. Hannah’s identification as Johanna remains probable. Some family trees give 1840 for Jacob’s birth; the date remains uncertain.

X_theresakryzer.note: Probable mother of Johanna Johns Rivers. Married Jacob Johns on 18 May 1868 according to his 1895 biography, which names twelve children. Her dates and parents are not established.

X_jacobjohnssr.note: Explicitly named father of Jacob Johns in his son's contemporary 1895 biography. Described as living in Winona County at age ninety-four. No exact birth date inferred. Both he and Maggie brought their son to America when he was three, landing at Baltimore, then living in Missouri and Hazel Green, Wisconsin before settling in Hart Township in 1856.

X_maggiejahn.note: Named as Maggie (Jahn) Johns, mother of Jacob Johns, in his 1895 biography. Her full given name, dates and birthplace are not established.

X_frederickbutturff.note: Named as Sarah Butturff Hall’s father in the 1884 biography of her husband George W. Hall. Pennsylvania association; no birth or death dates supplied. Samuel is explicitly Sarah’s brother, but the source does not separately state his parents.

X_elizabethbutturff.note: Named as Sarah Butturff Hall’s mother in the 1884 biography of George W. Hall. Her own maiden surname and dates are not supplied. Butturff is her married family name, not an established maiden name.

X_samuelbutturff.note: Explicitly Sarah Hall’s brother and George W. Hall’s furniture-store partner at Wabasha beginning in 1857. Parentage and dates are not separately stated in the source and are left blank.

X_ernestgustavbrose.note: Son of Ernest and Augusta Brose. World War I veteran and Northwestern Railway yardmaster, retired in September 1948. Married Lydia Zambrocki on 1 June 1949. Buried at Saint Mary’s Cemetery, Winona. These details appear in a transcription of the Winona Daily News notice of 2 June 1965, p. 7.

X_louisebrose.note: Daughter of Ernest and Augusta Brose. Married Max E. Schulze on 2 January 1911; their children were Arthur M. Schulze and Ruth Louise Urness. Buried at Woodlawn. The family relationships appear in a transcription of the Winona Daily News notice of 19 April 1962; the precise birth date comes from the memorial index.

X_minniebrose.note: Live memorial explicitly calls her daughter of Ernest/Augusta and wife of William Julius Schellhas. Independently named as sister in Ernest 1965 and Louise 1962 obituary transcriptions. Dates from memorial fields; burial Woodlawn.

X_idabrose.note: Identified as Ida Skow, a deceased sister, in Louise’s 1962 family notice. Parent links and dates are listed in her cemetery memorial; an original vital record is still needed for confirmation.

X_johnhbrose.note: Identified as a deceased brother in Louise’s 1962 family notice. Dates and parent links are listed in his cemetery memorial. Buried at Woodlawn, Section AA, Lot 66.

X_maxschulze.note: Husband of Louise Brose, married 2 January 1911. Her 1962 family notice records that he died in 1956.

X_williamschellhas.note: Named as Minnie Brose’s husband in her cemetery memorial biography. His birth year is given as 1883. The relationship remains probable pending a marriage record.

X_archwilliams.note: Birth and death years are on his grave marker. A transcribed contemporary obituary gives 27 November 1871 in Tennessee and names wife Fannie Racer and brothers Bud, Cleve and John. His placement as a son of Thomas and Rebecca remains probable.

X_williamhenrywilliams.note: The cemetery account gives 1870–1952 and an unmarked burial beside Maud. Arch’s family notice names a brother Bud; the family portrait caption names William. Identification and parentage remain probable.

X_johnarthurwilliams.note: Named John Arthur in the family caption for the back-left man in the five-brother portrait. Arch’s family notice names a surviving brother John Williams of Dallas. Identification and parentage remain probable; dates are unknown.

X_georgewilliams1891.note: Dates are legible on his grave marker. The family account identifies Thomas and Rebecca as his parents and places George at front right in the group photograph. Parentage remains probable. Accounts disagree about his marital status.

X_fannieracer.note: Original grave photograph confirms 1885–1963. Arch obituary explicitly names his wife as former Fannie Racer of Collinsville and says married 23 years before his death; exact wedding date not derived.

X_maudswett.note: Her marker names Maud, wife of W. H. Williams, born 17 May 1879 and died 18 October 1902. The surname Swett comes from the cemetery family account and remains probable.

X_katherineriversreiland.note: Daughter of Henry and Elizabeth (Lehnertz) Rivers. Married Michael N. Reiland on 20 August 1891. Distinct from Katherine Frisch, wife of Matthew Rivers.

X_michaelnreiland.note: Taught twelve years in Winona public schools before entering the general dry-goods business at Rollingstone in 1892. Had served ten years as village clerk by the 1913 biography and also as school treasurer.

X_peterreiland.note: Arrived in America in 1854 and married Christine Krier at Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, in 1857. Bought 80 acres in Norton Township in 1862 and expanded to 200; retired to Rollingstone in 1900. His exact Luxembourg birthplace is not specified.

X_christinekrier.note: Married Peter Reiland in 1857 at Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin; died in 1898. No parents or death place named in this source.

X_arthurpreiland.note: Teaching school in Winona County when the 1913 biography was published.

X_leonardjreiland.note: Working in the grocery business in Rollingstone in 1913.

X_adelaidereiland.note: Attending St. Mary Domestic Science School at Sparta, Wisconsin, in 1913.

X_lorendareiland.note: Living at home when the 1913 biography was published.

X_winifred_nelton_beeman.note: Her 1966 obituary gives 4 March 1882; a likely 1900 census entry gives March 1883 and later census ages also suggest 1883. The early record names Arthur O. Beeman’s wife Alvina; the identity is probable, and her mother’s name differs across the records.

X_audrey_johnson_king.note: Born to Joel Johnson and Winnie Bozarth; married Riley James King in Paris, Texas, on 29 December 1928.

X_riley_james_king.note: Rancher of Sterling City; married Audrey Johnson in 1928.

X_bonnie_ruth_king_alley.note: Daughter of Audrey Johnson and Riley King; married Marvin Eugene Alley in 1952.

X_marvin_eugene_alley.note: Farm supervisor in Saudi Arabia and later a Texas rancher and land appraiser.

X_robert_eugene_alley.note: Son of Bonnie Ruth King and Marvin Eugene Alley.

X_arthur_oscar_beeman.note: Husband of Winnie Nelton; the 1932 Minnesota death index and memorial list Arthur O. Beeman.

X_arthur_chester_beeman.note: Son of Winnie and Arthur O. Beeman; the dates are from a memorial index.

X_harold_oscar_beeman.note: Son of Winnie and Arthur O. Beeman; the dates are from a memorial index.

X_berniece_beeman_jaszewski.note: Daughter of Winnie and Arthur O. Beeman. The 1950 census records her as Bernice Raboin; her dates come from a memorial index.

X_john_canfield_senior.note: A John Canfield headed the Pennsylvania household containing John A., age two in 1850 and twelve in 1860, with Margaret and the same older children. Those censuses predate the relationship column, so the proposed father-son relationship is probable. His birth is estimated from the recorded ages, not an exact birth record.

X_anna_thompson_canfield.note: A Wabasha marriage index names John Canfield and Anna Thompson on 3 April 1884. The 1900 Kellogg household records a Norway-born Annie, married to John A. for sixteen years. The birth-register transcription identifies John and Anna as parents of Walter, Homer, Edith and Ruth. Matching the records remains probable; she is distinct from his first wife Anna Hall.

X_walter_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register records Walter, son of John and Anna, father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway; Walter H., fourteen, appears with John A. and Annie in 1900. On that basis he is probably James Garfield Canfield’s half-brother.

X_homer_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register records Homer, son of John and Anna, with father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway; Homer A., twelve, appears in John A. Canfield’s household in 1900. His later life is not established.

X_edith_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register records Edith B., daughter of John and Anna, father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway. The 1900 household has Edith aged ten, indexed with middle initial S.; the conflicting initial is left unresolved.

X_ruth_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register names Ruth Jean, daughter of John and Anna, father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway; Ruth J., seven, appears in John A. Canfield’s household in 1900. Her later life is not established.

X_marion_canfield.note: The original 1910 census names Marion, age two, as daughter of James and Helen Canfield; the original 1920 census lists Marian Canfield, eleven, with Nellie Miller and Helen Canfield. Her 1979 family notice identifies her as Marion E. Huntley, née Canfield, and names sister Helen Nelton. It reports her marriage in Winona on 22 July 1926 and her death on the Sunday before 27 November 1979.

X_tom_miller.note: The original 1920 Winona census names Tom Miller, 28, his wife Nellie, 33, and stepdaughters Marian and Helen Canfield. The names and ages support identifying Nellie with the widow of James Garfield Canfield. A marriage record and Tom’s later life have not been established.

X_john_h_heffernan.note: John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household names Nelly, Maudie, Kathy, Loy and Villy. Helen Miller’s obituary identifies siblings Maude Kling, Catherine Ley, Lloyd and William, and her 1939 Social Security application names John H. Heffernan and Mary Shea as her parents. Her 1948 death index instead records father Patrick Heffernan and mother Ellen Shea. The conflicting father’s name remains unresolved; this parental identification is probable.

X_mary_ellen_shea.note: The 1881 marriage certificate calls her Mary Ellen Shea; her 1903 obituary calls her Mary Helen Shea and names husband John Heffernan and their surviving children Helen, Katie, Loy, Maud and Willie. Her 1900 census entry records birth in Minnesota in March 1863; the obituary gives St. Louis in 1864. The 1903 death register gives parents indexed as Jermia Shay and Ellen Holliham. The 1914 death register of a man corresponding to her brother P. W. Shea gives Jeremiah Shea and Ellen Holland; the maternal surname readings differ. Helen’s 1939 application names John H. and Mary Shea as her parents, while Helen’s 1948 death index gives father Patrick Heffernan and mother Ellen Shea. Both generations remain probable with these conflicting details noted.

X_maude_heffernan.note: Maudie appears in the 1900 household of John and Mary. Helen Miller’s 1948 obituary names her sister Mrs. Michael Kling, and Maude Kling’s 1958 obituary names John Heffernan as her father. Maude’s obituary gives an 1891 birth and a 1909 marriage, while a 1910 census lists a Maude Hefferman as James Canfield’s single sister-in-law; that marital-status discrepancy remains unresolved.

X_catherine_heffernan.note: Kathy is recorded in John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household. Helen’s 1948 obituary names sister Mrs. John Ley, and Maude Kling’s 1958 obituary names sister Catherine Ley. The proposed relationship to these parents is probable.

X_lloyd_heffernan.note: Loy appears in John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household; Helen’s 1948 obituary names a brother Lloyd. In 1920 Lloyd J. Heffernan lived with Mike and Maud Kling next door to Tom and Nellie Miller. The parent link remains probable.

X_william_heffernan.note: Villy is listed in John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household, and Helen Miller’s 1948 obituary names her brother William. The connection and identity are probable; his later life has not been established.

X_jermia_shea.note: Mary Heffernan’s 1903 death-register index transcribes her father as Jermia Shay. Her family notice identifies her parents as Mr. and Mrs. J. Shea and her brother as P. W. Shea of Kellogg. Patrick W. Shea’s original 1914 death register names his father Jeremiah Shea. The records support the identification, which remains probable.

X_ellen_holliham.note: Mary Heffernan’s 1903 death-register index transcribes her mother as Ellen Holliham. Patrick W. Shea’s 1914 original death register names his mother Ellen Holland. Mary’s family notice identifies P. W. Shea as her brother; the two different surname readings remain unresolved.

X_frank_heffernan.note: Frank, seventeen, appears as a son in John and Mary Heffernan’s original 1900 census household. Mary’s 1903 notice says her eldest son died eleven weeks before her but does not name him, so that statement is not assigned to Frank without another record.

X_patrick_w_shea.note: Mary Heffernan’s 1903 obituary names her brother P. W. Shea of Kellogg. Patrick W. Shea’s 1914 death register records birthplace Missouri and parents Jeremiah Shea and Ellen Holland. His age and birth-date entries differ by about a year, so his birth is approximate. The identification is probable.

X_florence_minton.note: The 1920 census lists Florence Minton, 58, as mother-in-law of Joel Johnson, whose wife is indexed as Minnie. Their names, ages and children match the 1910 Joel and Winnie Johnson household. Florence’s earlier surname and spouse have not been established.

X_aletha_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records Aletha, age 12, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_porter_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records Porter, age 9, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_george_f_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records George, age 6, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_willie_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records Willie, age 4, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_frisch_anna_daughter.note: St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index names Anna as Jacob Frisch’s daughter in the same lot as Jacob and Annette. It does not explicitly name her mother; the link to Annette is probable.

X_frisch_alois.note: St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index calls Alois a son of Jacob and Annette, age two. The index marks his dates and grave location uncertain, so his exact birth and death are not established.

X_frisch_raymond.note: St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index identifies Raymond as the son of John and Margarite Frisch and gives his dates. The 1906 family notice describes an unnamed infant surviving Maggie; the dates make Raymond a plausible match.
